questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.
Be as plain as day.

options.text: Something is very clear, obvious, and easy to understand

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option(3)** i.e. **Something is very clear, obvious, and easy to understand**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **'Be as plain as day'** refers to something that is very **easy to see**, **perceive**, or **understand**; it is completely **obvious** and requires no proof. (**स्पष्ट होना**)
 
 
• **Example: **The reason for his resignation was **as plain as day** to everyone who worked with him.
 
 
 
• **'Something is very clear, obvious, and easy to understand'** defines the state of a fact or situation being **manifest** and **unmistakable**. (**कुछ बहुत स्पष्ट, प्रत्यक्ष और समझने में आसान होना**)
 
 
• **Example: **The instructions were **as plain as day**, yet he still managed to make a mistake.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the correct meaning of the idiom is **'something is very clear, obvious, and easy to understand'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **Something is very clear, obvious, and easy to understand**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Very different from the other** (एक दूसरे से बहुत अलग): Used to describe two things that have no similarities.
 
 
• **Example:** Although they are twins, their personalities are **very different from each other**.
 
 
 
• **In very good spirits** (बहुत प्रसन्न या उत्साहित): Feeling happy, lively, and optimistic.
 
 
• **Example:** The team was **in very good spirits** after winning the championship.
 
 
 
• **Very happy in thought** (विचारों में बहुत खुश): Being in a state of mental joy or pleasant contemplation.
 
 
• **Example:** She sat by the window, **very happy in thought** while remembering her childhood.

questions.question:
From the alternatives given below, select the correct meaning of the idiom.
Dangle a carrot in front of someone.

options.text: To try to entice one with the promise of a reward
To be very compatible and congenial together
An incentivization method in which a reward and a punishment are simultaneously offered/threatened as a motivation to complete some task
A person with red orange hair

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option (1)** i.e. **'To try to entice one with the promise of a reward'**.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **'Dangle a carrot in front of someone'** means to tempt or entice someone by promising a reward in exchange for their cooperation or hard work. (किसी को लालच देकर लुभाना)
 
 
• **Example: **The boss decided to **dangle a carrot** in front of his employees by promising a huge bonus if they met the year-end targets.
 
 
 
• **'To try to entice one with the promise of a reward'** is the direct meaning of the idiom, where the 'carrot' represents the incentive being offered. (किसी को इनाम के वादे से लुभाने की कोशिश करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The tech giant **dangled a carrot** of stock options in front of the lead developer to prevent him from joining a rival firm.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the meaning of the idiom is to entice someone with a reward.

Therefore, the correct answer is- **To try to entice one with the promise of a reward**.

**Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **To be very compatible and congenial together** (एक दूसरे के साथ बहुत अनुकूल और मिलनसार होना): Refers to people who get along very well.
 
 
• **Example:** The two musicians found they were very **compatible** and started a band together.
 
 
 
• **An incentivization method in which a reward and a punishment are simultaneously offered** (प्रोत्साहन और दंड की नीति): This is specifically known as the **'carrot and stick'** approach.
 
 
• **Example: **The government used a **carrot and stick** approach to enforce the new tax laws.
 
 
 
• **A person with red orange hair** (लाल नारंगी बालों वाला व्यक्ति): A literal description often associated with the word 'ginger' or 'carrot-top'.
 
 
• **Example:** Since he was a **person with red orange hair**, his friends nicknamed him Rusty.

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
Will we have shipped all the orders by the end of the day?

options.text: Will all the orders be shipped by us by the end of the day?
Will all the orders had been shipped by us by the end of the day?
Will all the orders have been shipped by us by the end of the day?
Will all the orders shipped by us by the end of the day?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Will all the orders have been shipped by us by the end of the day?**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is an **interrogative sentence** in the **Future Perfect Tense**. The active voice structure is: **Will** + **Subject** (we) + **have** + **V3** (shipped) + **Object** (all the orders)?

• To convert a **Future Perfect** sentence into **Passive Voice**, the construction follows this rule: **Will** + **Object** (new subject) + **have been** + **V3** (Past Participle) + **by + Agent**?

• In the transformation, the object **all the orders** takes the position of the subject, and the subject **we** is converted into its objective case **us** acting as the agent.

• The phrase **have been shipped** is the correct passive form for the perfect aspect, ensuring that the completion of the action in the future is properly conveyed.

• The time-related phrase **by the end of the day** remains unchanged at the end of the sentence to maintain the original meaning and context.

 **Additional Information__**

• Analysis of incorrect options:

• **Future Indefinite Passive**: Option 1 uses **be shipped**, which is the structure for **Simple Future Passive**, failing to reflect the perfective aspect (have + V3).

• **Grammatical Incompatibility**: Option 2 incorrectly uses **had been**. The modal verb **will** must be followed by the base form **have**, never the past form **had**.

• **Incomplete Verb Phrase**: Option 4 is missing the essential auxiliary verbs **have been**, rendering the sentence grammatically fragmented.

• The **Future Perfect Tense** is utilized to describe an event that is expected or planned to happen before a particular time in the future, typically indicated by the preposition **by**.
</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
By next summer, the builders will have completed the tower.

options.text: The tower has been completed by the builders by next summer.
The tower will be completed by the builders by next summer.
The tower will have been completed by the builders by next summer.
The tower was completed by the builders by next summer.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The tower will have been completed by the builders by next summer**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The given sentence 'By next summer, the builders will have completed the tower' is in the **Active Voice** and follows the **Future Perfect Tense** structure.

• The active structure for this tense is: **Subject + will have + Past Participle (V3) + Object**. In this sentence, **the builders** is the subject, **will have completed** is the verb, and **the tower** is the object.

• To convert a **Future Perfect** sentence into **Passive Voice**, the structure used is: **New Subject (Object of active) + will have been + Past Participle (V3) + by + New Object (Subject of active)**.

• Following this rule, **the tower** moves to the subject position, the auxiliary verb becomes **will have been**, and the main verb **completed** remains in its **V3** form.

• The phrase **by next summer** is an **Adverbial of Time** indicating a deadline in the future, which remains unchanged in position or tense during the conversion.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Future Perfect Tense** (Passive):

• It emphasizes the **completion** of an action before a specific point in the future rather than the doer of the action.

• The inclusion of **been** is mandatory to distinguish the passive form from the active future perfect.

• Distinguishing other Tenses:

• **Simple Future Passive**: Uses **will be + V3** (e.g., 'The tower will be completed'). This lacks the 'completion by a deadline' nuance.

• **Present Perfect Passive**: Uses **has/have been + V3** (e.g., 'The tower has been completed'). This refers to an action already finished in the past with current relevance.

• **Simple Past Passive**: Uses **was/were + V3** (e.g., 'The tower was completed'). This indicates the action occurred at a specific time in the past.

</ul

questions.question:
In the given question, a sentence is divided into four parts and given in the alternatives (A), (B), (C), and (D). There is an error in one part. Choose the alternative containing that part of the sentence that has the error. Choosing the alternative with the error will be the answer.
I want to spend some time in the forest passing with trees and enjoying the natural beauty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**forest passing with trees**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence involves identifying a grammatical or semantic error within its segments. Part (1) **I want to spend** is grammatically accurate as it uses the standard **Subject + Verb + to-infinitive** pattern. Hence, statement 1 is correct.
 
• Part (2) **some time in the** correctly applies the quantifier **some** before the uncountable noun **time** and initiates a prepositional phrase to indicate location. Hence, statement 2 is correct.
 
• Part (3) **forest passing with trees** is the erroneous segment. The use of the preposition **with** after the participle **passing** is semantically incorrect in this context. Trees are stationary biological entities; therefore, one cannot **pass with** them. The intended meaning suggests movement **through** the forest or being **surrounded by** trees. The correct prepositional usage for traversing a wooded area is **passing through**. Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.
 
• Part (4) **and enjoying the natural beauty** maintains grammatical consistency by using the **present participle** form (**enjoying**) to describe an action occurring while spending time in the forest. Hence, statement 4 is correct.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Prepositions of Movement and Place**:
 
 
• **Through**: Specifically used when moving within a three-dimensional space or an area filled with objects, such as a **forest**, a crowd, or a tunnel.
 
• **Among**: Used when one is in the middle of or surrounded by multiple distinct entities, such as **among the trees**.
 
 
 
• **Participle Phrases**:
 
 
• The words **passing** and **enjoying** function as participles that modify how the subject intends to **spend time**.
 
• Proper **parallelism** requires that multiple activities linked by a conjunction (like **and**) share the same grammatical structure to ensure sentence flow and clarity.
 
 
</ul

Select the correct alternative to fill in the blank with the correct preposition in the following sentence.

Alexander had a genius ________ tactical warfare.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**for**'. **__Key Points__** __ 
• The noun **genius**, when used to describe a natural ability, talent, or exceptional aptitude, is idiomatically followed by the preposition **for**. 
• The phrase **genius for** indicates that someone has a special talent for a particular activity or subject. 
• In the given sentence, **Alexander** is described as having an exceptional talent for **tactical warfare**. Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**. **Complete Sentence:** *'Alexander had a **genius for**__ tactical warfare.'* **__Additional Information__** 
• **Option 2: in** is occasionally used to denote a field of study (e.g., **a genius in mathematics**), but **for** is the standard preposition for specific skills or actions. 
• **Option 3: of** is used to show possession or origin (e.g., **the genius of Mozart**) rather than the talent someone possesses for a task. 
• **Option 4: to** is grammatically incorrect in this context. </ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: "No Improvement Required."

The committee concluded that the measures suggested were __conducive in bring stability in__ the financial system.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**conducive to bringing stability to**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The adjective **conducive** means making a certain situation or outcome likely or possible. In English grammar, it is a **fixed collocation** that this word is always followed by the preposition **to**. Therefore, phrases like 'conducive in' or 'conducive of' are idiomatic errors.

• When the word **to** acts as a preposition (as it does following the adjective 'conducive'), any subsequent verb must be in the **gerund form** (verb + ing). This explains why **bringing** is required instead of the base form 'bring'.

• The phrase **bring stability to** is the standard idiomatic construction used to indicate the recipient or the system affected by the stabilization. The preposition **to** correctly identifies the **financial system** as the entity receiving the benefit of the measures.

• The original sentence is incorrect because it uses the preposition 'in' after 'conducive', fails to use the **gerund** form of the verb, and uses the wrong preposition before 'the financial system'.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Prepositional Idioms:**

• Certain adjectives require specific prepositions to be grammatically correct. Examples include **detrimental to**, **beneficial to**, and **immune to**.

• **Conducive to** is frequently used in formal reports and academic writing to describe factors that contribute to a desired environment or result, such as **economic growth** or **peace**.

• **Gerund vs. Infinitive:**

• Learners often mistake the **prepositional to** for the **infinitive marker to**. In phrases like 'look forward to', 'object to', or 'conducive to', the word **to** is a preposition and must be followed by a **noun** or **gerund**.

• Example: 'The environment is **conducive to** learning' (Noun) or 'The environment is **conducive to** studying' (Gerund).

</ul

questions.question:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

Since the people who gave me a ride decided to leave the concert early, __so I had to take a bus home__.

options.text: so I had taken a bus home
I had to take a bus home
so I had to get a bus home

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary grammatical error in the sentence is the redundant use of the conjunction ‘**so**’ after the subordinating conjunction ‘**Since**’.
 
• In English grammar, words like **Since**, **Because**, and **As** introduce a reason (subordinate clause). When a sentence starts with these words, the result (main clause) should follow after a comma without another conjunction like ‘**so**’ or ‘**therefore**’.
 
• Using both ‘**Since**’ and ‘**so**’ in the same sentence is a common error known as **double conjunction** or **redundancy**.
 
• Removing the word ‘**so**’ makes the sentence grammatically sound: ‘Since the people... early, **I had to take a bus home**.’
 
• Therefore, **Option 2** is the correct replacement.

Therefore, the correct answer is **I had to take a bus home**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *‘Since the people who gave me a ride decided to leave the concert early, **I had to take a bus home**.’*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** ‘**so I had taken a bus home**’ – This retains the redundant ‘**so**’ and unnecessarily changes the tense to **past perfect**, which does not fit the context of the simple past sequence.
 
• **Option 3:** ‘**so I had to get a bus home**’ – This also retains the redundant ‘**so**’, making it grammatically incorrect regardless of the verb change from ‘take’ to ‘get’.
 
• **Option 4:** ‘**No improvement required**’ – This is incorrect because the original sentence contains a **redundancy error**.
 
• Similar rules apply to **Although/Though**; you should not use ‘**but**’ in the same sentence (e.g., ‘Although it was raining, but he went out’).
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following statements most accurately encapsulates the central idea of the passage?

options.text: Demanding more rapid and widely shared economic growth
Focusing only on achieving substantial economic growth
Improving India's global standing for economic growth
Ensuring equitable distribution of wealth by the government

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage emphasizes that although **India** has grown fast, it has the potential to develop even **faster** and more effectively.
 
• The core theme is the concept of **inclusive growth**, which is defined as growth that distributes economic gains across the **entire population** rather than a specific group.
 
• The author argues that growth should be viewed as an **instrument for spreading prosperity** to all segments of society, particularly the **poorest segment**.
 
• By advocating for both an increase in the pace of development and a broader distribution of its benefits, **Option 1** most accurately captures the central idea.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Demanding more rapid and widely shared economic growth**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** This is incorrect because the passage explicitly mentions that high growth alone is **not a sufficient condition** for eradicating poverty.
 
• **Option 3:** While global standing is mentioned as a point of comparison, it is not the **defining concept** or goal discussed in the text.
 
• **Option 4:** While the government's role in redistribution is mentioned, the passage focuses more broadly on the nature of **economic growth** itself as a tool for inclusive progress.
 
• The passage suggests measuring success through the **per capita income** and **growth rate** of the **bottom 20 per cent** of the population.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following definitions most accurately describes the concept of "inclusive growth"?

options.text: Growth that serves only the wealthiest
Growth that improves society as a whole
Growth that sidelines the poorest in pursuit of economic progress
Growth oriented on creating industries and increasing infrastructure

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the passage, **inclusive growth** is defined by the distribution of economic gains to the **entire population** rather than a specific group.
 
• The text emphasizes that growth should be treated as an instrument for **spreading prosperity to all** citizens, which aligns with the idea of improving **society as a whole**.
 
• It highlights that progress should be measured by the advancement of the **poorest segment** (the bottom 20 per cent), ensuring that no one is left behind.
 
• The participation of the **poor segment** and the existence of **redistribution mechanisms** for the vulnerable are central to this concept.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because the passage explicitly rejects focusing on a **specific group** (like the wealthy) and instead promotes growth for the **entire population**.
 
• **Option 3** is incorrect because the passage states that growth must include the **participation of the poor** rather than **sideline** them.
 
• **Option 4** is incorrect because, while **industries and infrastructure** are drivers of economic development, the "inclusive" aspect specifically refers to how the **benefits** of that development are shared across **all levels of society**.
</ul

questions.question: What is necessary to eradicate poverty?

options.text: Eradicating poverty only by achieving high economic growth
Redistributing wealth to only the richest segments
Combining economic growth with the participation of the poor
Addressing poverty exclusively through market-driven policies

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explicitly states that while **economic growth** is necessary for eradicating poverty, it is **not a sufficient condition** on its own.
 
• It emphasizes that policies designed for growth must ensure that the **poor segment** of the population is enabled to **participate** in the economic process.
 
• Additionally, the concept of **inclusive growth** requires **mechanisms** to be in place to **redistribute** the economic gains to **vulnerable** individuals.
 
• Thus, the eradication of poverty depends on the synergy between **achieving growth** and ensuring the **active participation of the poor**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Combining economic growth with the participation of the poor**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is incorrect because the passage clarifies that growth is a necessary but **not a sufficient condition**; it cannot solve poverty in isolation.
 
• **Option 2** is incorrect as the primary goal of **inclusive growth** is to distribute gains to the **entire population**, particularly the **bottom 20 per cent**, rather than focusing on the rich.
 
• **Option 4** is incorrect because the text suggests the need for specific **policy interventions** and **redistributive mechanisms**, which goes beyond purely **market-driven policies**.
</ul

questions.question: What are the two corollaries of inclusive growth mentioned in the passage?

options.text: High growth and benefits for the weakest segments

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage defines **inclusive growth** as a concept where economic gains are distributed to the **entire population** rather than being confined to a specific group.
 
• It emphasizes that **economic growth** should not be seen as an end in itself but as an **instrument** for spreading prosperity to all members of society.
 
• According to the text, for growth to be truly inclusive, it requires the **participation of the poor segment** and mechanisms to **redistribute gains** to those who are vulnerable.
 
• Thus, the two fundamental corollaries mentioned or implied are achieving **high growth** and ensuring that the **weakest segments** (the bottom 20 percent) benefit from that progress.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Low inflation and high employment:** While these are positive economic indicators, the passage focuses specifically on the **distribution of wealth** and the **participation of the poor** in the growth process.
 
• **Privatization and foreign investment:** These are methods to stimulate the economy, but the passage defines inclusive growth through the **lens of equity** and social welfare rather than specific market mechanisms.
 
• **Market reforms and tax reduction:** These are policy instruments, whereas the passage identifies the **metric of success** as the per capita income of the **bottom quintile** of the population.
</ul

questions.question: According to the passage, which metric is proposed for measuring inclusive growth?

options.text: By total exports and imports in a fiscal year
Per capita income of the bottom 20%
By the growth in the urban employment rate

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• The passage explores the concept of **inclusive growth**, emphasizing that economic success should be measured by how it affects the entire population.
 
• According to the text, a nation's progress should be evaluated based on its **poorest segment** rather than the average or total growth alone.
 
• The specific metric proposed is the **per capita income of the bottom 20%** (also referred to as the bottom quintile) of the population.
 
• By calculating the **growth rate of income** for this specific group, the government can determine if prosperity is truly being spread widely.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **GDP growth rate**: The passage mentions that while India has grown fast, growth is an **instrument** and not a sufficient condition for **poverty eradication** on its own.
 
• **Bottom Quintile**: In statistics, a quintile represents **20%** of a given population; the **bottom quintile** specifically refers to the lowest-earning group.
 
• **Redistribution**: The passage suggests that for growth to be inclusive, there must be mechanisms to **redistribute gains** to the **vulnerable segments** of society.
</ul
